newsitem.title: USA: Consumer body wants PacTel plan safeguards.
newsitem.headline: Consumer body wants PacTel plan safeguards.

text.p: A consumer advocates' body said on Friday that safeguards should be adopted to protect Pacific Bell customers before a sister company is allowed to provide long-distance service in California.

The Office of Ratepayer Advocates of the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) said Pacific Bell customers could be harmed substantially if Pacific Bell Communications' (PBCOM) application to offer local and long-distance services in California is approved as submitted.

The office is an independent arm of the CPUC that represents consumers' interests before the commission, the state utility regulator. Pacific Bell, a unit of Pacific Telesis Group, now provides local service to about 15 million lines in California.
Under the Federal Telecommunications Act of 1996, Pacific Telesis may provide long-distance services through a separate, unregulated subsidiary, PBCOM, once it meets certain conditions.
PBCOM asked for CPUC approval to provide long-distance and local service in California in direct competition with Pacific Bell, according to the Office of Ratepayer Advocates.

The office said that because Pacific Bell is an affiliate of PBCOM, there should be "specific safeguards to ensure that Pacific Bell and its customers are protected from financial and competitive risks associated with PBCOM's application."
It said Pacific Bell should be prevented from making "inappropriate transactions" with PBCOM such as transferring employees and giving customer information to PBCOM.

PBCOM should be limited to providing only local services that it purchases from Pacific Bell, and Pacific Bell should receive an "appropriate compensation" for activities it carries out on PBCOM's behalf, it said.
PBCOM is to file a reply on November 14. Hearings are to begin December 2 and a final decision by the CPUC is expected in the second quarter of 1997.
